clue.text: Treat dad gave - and it's in unfavourable circumstances

indicators.note: to treat something is to process or work on it, so the following letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: all the letters of these four words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A child wonders whether a treat from father came with hidden strings attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat' reads as a noun, a present from dad, but it is the verb telling you to rearrange the next thirteen letters into DISADVANTAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disadvantaged is placed in poor or unfavourable conditions, so the adjective and the phrase describe the same situation.

clue.text: Club team's one with great stamina

blocks.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a team is a side; the possessive 's supplies the final S

explanation.surface: A sports club praises one member of its team for exceptional endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: IRON plus SIDES gives IRONSIDES; 'team's' reads as a possessive but it stands for the plural SIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironsides is a nickname for a person of great physical toughness and bravery, famously Cromwell and his cavalry.

clue.text: Cancel a missing yearbook

indicators.note: missing says the yearbook goes without one of its letters, the one named just before

blocks.note: the letter A, taken as written, which is removed
an annual is a book published once a year

explanation.surface: A school cancels its yearbook because it has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ANNUAL and remove one A to leave ANNUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to declare it void, which is to cancel it officially.

clue.text: Upset in grave kind of pickle

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters that follow are scrambled

blocks.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed at finding themselves in a grave sort of predicament, a pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like the slang for a fix, matching 'grave', but here it is the food preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is the sour liquid used for pickling, and onions or eggs preserved in it count as pickles.

clue.text: Short letter showing that school raised rent

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the school's name is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English public school
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A brief letter announces that a school has put up its rent.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON read upwards gives NOTE, followed by LET, making NOTELET. 'Raised rent' looks like a rent rise, but 'raised' belongs to the school.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet or card for writing a brief message, so a short letter.

clue.text: I go for it!

blocks.note: surface reading: an exclamation of bold resolve before taking a risk
setter's reading: what a person seeking a job or place says of the post they put in for

explanation.walkthrough: To go for a job is to apply for it, so the speaker is someone making an application.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant is a person who formally asks for a job, place or grant, that is, who goes for it.

clue.text: The high flier seen round one particular machine

indicators.note: seen round means the bird is placed around the next item, enclosing it

blocks.note: the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword favourite
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soaring bird is spotted circling one specific contraption.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNE round I gives ERNIE. ERNIE is the British computer that draws the winning Premium Bond numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: ERNIE, the Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment, is one specific named device, hence a particular machine.

clue.text: If you can do this, there's no further argument

definitions.text: If you can do this, there's no further argument

blocks.clueFragment: If you can do this, there's no further argument
blocks.note: surface reading: it seems to describe settling a dispute by one side winning

blocks.clueFragment: If you can do this, there's no further argument
blocks.note: setter's reading: the dispute ends with both sides keeping their views and simply stopping

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests reaching agreement, but the twist is that the parties agree only that they disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both parties accept their opinions will not converge and drop the quarrel, ending further debate.

clue.text: Scenic tone is seen initially, working to provide harmonies

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
working suggests letters set in motion and rearranged into a new form

blocks.note: these three words taken as written
the first letter of seen

explanation.surface: A description of a landscape painting whose scenic tones work together harmoniously.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters of 'Scenic tone is' plus S make CONSISTENCIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Consistencies are agreements or compatibilities between parts, so they are harmonies in the sense of things fitting together.

clue.text: Prepared teachers in North American plant

blocks.note: ground as in coffee or spice that has been milled ready for use
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers

explanation.surface: Trained teachers are posted out to North America.
explanation.walkthrough: GROUND plus NUT makes GROUNDNUT. The NUT was Britain's main teachers' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundnut, Apios americana, is a climbing vine native to North America with edible tubers.

clue.text: Peter's mostly top in Christmas production

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the following word is dropped

blocks.note: Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up; the 's reads as 'is'
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: Peter is almost the star in a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto, short for pantomime, is the British family stage comedy put on around Christmas; Peter Pan is itself a classic panto story.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomimes are staged chiefly in the Christmas and New Year season in Britain, so a panto is a Christmas production.

clue.text: A contribution to please lively art supporter

indicators.note: a contribution is a part given towards a whole, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

blocks.note: found inside letters 3-7 of 'please lively'

explanation.surface: Someone donates to brighten up an arts venue and support lively art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art supporter' sounds like a patron, but it is the wooden stand that holds a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame that holds up a canvas while it is painted or displayed, so it literally supports art.

clue.text: Swift work

blocks.note: surface reading: a job done quickly
setter's reading: a book written by the satirist Jonathan Swift

explanation.walkthrough: The capital S is hidden at the start of the clue; Swift is the eighteenth-century Irish author, and his best-known work is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift wrote the 1726 satire about Lemuel Gulliver's voyages to Lilliput and other lands, his most famous book.

clue.text: A tot? One finds difficulty in walking

blocks.note: first meaning: a very young child
second meaning: one who moves with short unsteady steps

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same small child, first by age and then by the wobbly gait that gives the word its origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a young child just learning to walk, who totters along unsteadily, so both a tot and an unsteady walker.

clue.text: Ways of escaping from flight manoeuvres round space

indicators.note: round means the manoeuvres are wrapped around the next word

blocks.note: loops are aerobatic manoeuvres in flight
a hole is an empty space or gap

explanation.surface: A pilot evades pursuit by looping around in open sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight manoeuvres' and 'escaping' suggest one aerial scene, but the escape is from rules and the flight only supplies wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopholes are gaps in rules that let people evade obligations, and originally narrow slits in a wall, so ways out.

clue.text: See 13
It's not good for the viewers

definitions.text: It's not good for the viewers

blocks.clueFragment: It's not good for the viewers
blocks.note: surface reading: a programme unsuitable for a television audience

blocks.clueFragment: It's not good for the viewers
blocks.note: setter's reading: viewers are the organs we see with, and this harms them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewers' suggests a TV audience, but here it means the eyes themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is tiredness and discomfort of the eyes from overuse, something plainly bad for the organs of sight.

clue.text: Possibly sip in prescribed amount to order

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements of the short word that follows
in places the rearranged letters inside the amount

blocks.note: the letters of sip, rearranged
a dose is a measured amount of medicine

explanation.surface: A patient takes small sips of a prescribed amount of medicine as ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is a verb here, meaning arrange, not a doctor's instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispose things is to arrange or set them out in a particular way, as troops are disposed, so to order them.

clue.text: Variety of oriental nut oil washing out with solvent

indicators.note: a variety is a different form of something, so the following letters appear in a new order

blocks.note: E for eastern
the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of Asian nut oil is used to clean something with a solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus a rearrangement of NUT OIL gives ELUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, elution is the extraction of one substance from another by washing it through with a solvent.

clue.text: End of half surviving army unit

indicators.note: half means only the first three of the six letters of the next word are kept

blocks.note: extant means still in existence
REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: The fate of half the survivors of a military unit is grimly described.
explanation.walkthrough: EXT(ANT) plus REME gives EXTREME. REME is a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an extreme is the furthest point or limit of something, so its end.

clue.text: Endless dinner, for instance, without starter but including bird

indicators.note: without starter means the first letter of the instance is removed
including means the remainder holds the bird inside it

blocks.note: dinner is an example of a meal
the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A dinner seems to go on forever, lacking a first course yet including poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: (M)EAL holds TERN: E(TERN)AL. 'Endless dinner' suggests a long meal, but 'Endless' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts forever without beginning or end, so it is endless.

clue.text: Use for ham (sliced) in a kind of loaf

indicators.note: sliced means cut up, so the letters are chopped and reassembled

blocks.note: all three words taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for using sliced ham in a sandwich loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: A farmhouse loaf is a British white bread baked in a tin, with a split, floury top.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmhouse is a style of bread loaf sold in Britain, so the word names a kind of loaf.

clue.text: Regret holding exercises for money

indicators.note: holding means the first word keeps the second inside it

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Someone regrets the money spent on gym exercise classes.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE holds PE: RU(PE)E.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India, Pakistan and several other countries, so it is a form of money.

clue.text: Act it in play? It's exposed, if you raise the roof

definitions.text: It's exposed, if you raise the roof

indicators.note: in play means the letters are in motion and freely rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: A stage direction to act something out, followed by the idea of raising the roof in a lively show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise the roof' suggests loud applause, but taken literally, lifting the roof off a house uncovers the room just beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The attic lies directly under the roof, so it would be laid bare if the roof were physically lifted away.

clue.text: Tsar rashly providing a tapestry

indicators.note: providing means the words supply the answer from within themselves

blocks.note: found inside letters 3-7 of 'Tsar rashly'

explanation.surface: An impulsive Russian ruler hastily hands over a wall hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a rich woven wall hanging, named after the French town where such cloths were made.

clue.text: Drive out protest leader in river with line

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of the word before it
in places that single letter inside the river

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
the first letter of protest
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Authorities expel the leader of a protest found by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England; 'leader' looks like a person to throw out but only picks a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force someone or something out, as a pupil from school, so to drive it out.

clue.text: Central tax (English) to provide causes of sensation

blocks.note: inner means at the centre
VAT is value added tax
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A central tax levied in England is meant to create a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: INNER plus VAT plus E gives INNERVATE; the causes of sensation are nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: To innervate an organ is to supply it with nerves, and nerves are what carry sensation.

clue.text: Role passing in moves focusing on individual qualities

indicators.note: moves means the letters shift position into a new order

blocks.note: all three words taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor's role is passed on through a series of moves on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In moves' reads as one phrase, but 'in' belongs to the letters and 'moves' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Personalising something tailors it to a particular person, so it concentrates on that individual's own qualities.
